title: Agent Spaghetti integration manifest, version 1 (ADR 0004, ADR 0008)

abilities.description: what the tool's agent can do beyond answering from what its model knows: web = it can search and read the web (tasks that need it go there first)

color.description: the tool's own color in activity lines (Live, Activity); without it the tool gets one of the UI's tool colors. Keep it clear of the action colors (red, gold, green)

processNotIn.description: Path fragments of copies bundled inside other tools (e.g. LM Studio's own llama-server): such processes are not this tool

paths.description: default places of its program (globs; %VAR% and ~ expanded); {installed}/… = inside an install the OS lists (e.g. a Store app's folder)

url.description: a hosted API: probed at this address (with speaks.openai.headers) once its detect.env variables are set; never by the live poll

uses.description: the model the tool is set to use, read from its own config file (JSON or JSONC); free: the free model a task passes when none is set

model.description: dotted path; {key} is the value of that key at the file's root

order.description: which local model server is used when several have a model loaded: lowest first, one at a time

headers.description: sent with every request (probe and run); {env:NAME} is read from the environment at request time (NAME must be in detect.env)

openaiClient.description: the tool can use a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint: the model gateway

setup.description: steps for the user; {url} and {key} are filled in; the tool asks for model auto and Agent Spaghetti picks (Tools → Model)

auto.description: connect sets the gateway up by itself (gateway on): our entry in the tool's JSON list of model providers, settings it needs

config.description: the JSON file holding a list of model providers

entry.description: our provider entry, found again by name; {url} and {key} are filled in

settings.description: settings it needs, added to a JSON settings file where the user has not set them

chat.description: its chat takes a task: <command…> <prompt> - (task on stdin); results come back through report

entry.description: extra fields our server entry needs, e.g. { "type": "stdio" }

commandArray.description: the entry's command holds the program and its arguments as one array

mcpCli.description: the tool's own CLI adds/removes MCP servers: <bin> <add…> agent-spaghetti -- <command…> / <bin> <remove…> agent-spaghetti

config.description: a non-JSON config file the CLI writes; connected = it names our server

mcpClientNames.description: its MCP clientInfo name(s), matched case-insensitively

agentFile.description: path of the agent-spaghetti custom agent file connect writes (the tool's user agents folder)

agentModel.description: the agent file's model line, verbatim in the tool's syntax: the agent's preferred model (e.g. the gateway's, which connect sets up)

agentTools.description: the agent file's tools line, verbatim in the tool's syntax (e.g. VS Code: ['agent-spaghetti/*']): the agent then only hands off; without, it has the tool's default tools

promptHook.description: the >> shortcut through the tool's prompt hook: hooks.<event>[] in a JSON settings file
